note: First-time guide. One entry per screen; each shows once, then can be replayed from the Tips button. A step with no 'anchor' is a modal in the middle of the screen. A step with an 'anchor' (a CSS selector) points at that part of the page and outlines it. Plain words only: say what Plainflow is making and doing, not what the buttons are called. 'canvas' shows after the picture draws; 'answer' shows after Check it.

door.title: What this does
door.body: Describe a proposal that uses personal data in one sentence, then answer a few questions. Plainflow turns that into a diagram of where the data goes and reads the answer from it: whether it can go ahead, whether your organisation's policy allows it, whether a DPIA is needed (a written assessment of what could go wrong for people), and what to do next.
door.aside: Nothing you type is sent anywhere; it stays in this browser until you save it. Use roles and groups, never people's names.

door.title: Start here
door.body: Say what you are checking: a new proposal, something already in use, a sensitivity level you already know, or an app you have built. Choose one and a sentence to complete appears below.

questions.title: A few questions, then the diagram
questions.body: Plainflow is building a diagram of your proposal. Each answer sets something on it. Some answers are suggested from your sentence; change anything that is wrong.
questions.aside: There are no wrong answers. A yes means a closer look, not a no.

questions.title: Tick what's true
questions.body: A list like this stands in for a series of yes or no questions. The note under each item explains what it means. If you are not sure, skip it and the suggestion stands.

questions.title: The answer, forming
questions.body: This updates as you answer. Nothing here is final until a person signs it.

canvas.title: Your proposal, as a diagram
canvas.body: Each box is one part of the proposal: the people concerned, the data, the tool, the purpose, and the companies that handle the data. Connections show where data goes; the thick amber ones carry personal data. The dashed line is the boundary of your organisation: anything to the right of it is outside.
canvas.aside: You can drag boxes about, and nothing you do here is final.

canvas.title: The sentence is the diagram
canvas.body: Hover over a word to highlight where that data goes. Select one to open its box.

canvas.title: When it looks right
canvas.body: Review the diagram first. Then select this and Plainflow reads the answer from it: whether it can go ahead, whether policy allows it, and what to do next.

screening.title: The form your DPO signs
screening.body: Everything here comes from your diagram: the screening questions with the reason for each answer, the data's level, and what still needs a person. You do not need to read it; it is here for your DPO.

rules.title: How the answers are worked out
rules.body: Every answer Plainflow gives comes from this table, not from hidden code. It is here so a DPO can check a rule and change it. You do not need to read it unless you want to see why something was said.

compare.title: Two versions side by side
compare.body: A is the copy you pinned; B is the diagram as it is now. What changed is listed, and the to-do list shows what each version needs. Keep A, or proceed with B.

answer.title: The answer, read from the diagram
answer.body: Everything on the right comes from the diagram: whether it can go ahead, the facts behind that, and a list of actions. From now on it is live: change the diagram and the answer changes with it.
answer.aside: Nothing here is final until a person signs it.

answer.title: Change any setting
answer.body: The settings on each box are the choices you made in the questions. Change one and the answer updates immediately, and a box on the right explains what changed. Hover over a setting to see what it means.

answer.title: Your answer
answer.body: Whether it can go ahead, in plain words, then the facts behind it: the data, policy, and whether a DPIA is needed. Select a fact to see why.

answer.title: What to do
answer.body: Each line is one action needed before this goes ahead, with who does it and roughly how long it takes. Select a line to see what it is and why it is there.

answer.title: Tools
answer.body: Add a box and it arrives connected, so the answer changes immediately. Undo reverses anything. Tidy the layout, fold boxes to their titles, or pin a copy to compare two versions.

answer.title: Save, and the record
answer.body: Finish gives you the pages to take away: one for you, the record for your DPO, and a note for next time. Save keeps the diagram as a file you can open again.

report.title: What the code shows
report.body: This is everything the scan found in the code, with the exact lines as evidence, and what each finding does not prove. It is the raw material. The answer that counts is on the Canvas, where your answers fill in what code cannot tell.
report.aside: Each card opens to show the code and the reasoning.

pack.title: What you leave with
pack.body: Three pages from the same diagram: one for you (whether it can go ahead, and the steps), the record your DPO signs, and a note for whoever picks this up next. Print any page to PDF, copy it all as text for an email, or save the file to reopen the diagram.
pack.aside: Nothing here is final until a person signs it.
